title: New insights into single-grain mechanical behavior from temperature-dependent 3-D coherent X-ray diffraction

nodes.label: How strain heterogeneity inside one grain of a polycrystal evolves under load, and how its neighbours set it, has not been imaged in 3-D in situ
Coherent X-ray diffraction with a 2x2 um beam on one isolated grain during in-situ thermal cycling, with phase retrieval of its 3-D displacement field
Polycrystalline Au film chosen for high X-ray scattering power, large elastic anisotropy and oxidation resistance
Locate the diffracting grain by comparing an EBSD orientation map with a {111} high-resolution pole figure of the same FIB-isolated 15x15 um island
Temperature from room temperature to about 270 C and back in 25 C steps (about 0.03% mismatch strain per step), over successive cycles
Physical vapour deposition of a 475 nm Au film on fused silica
Flame anneal 30 s at 800-900 C to grow the grains laterally
Grains are columnar: boundaries run through the whole film thickness
Film has a strong {111} fibre texture: nearly all grains <111> out-of-plane, a few <100> grains
Before loading the grain already carries strong strain heterogeneity, in-plane and mainly along y, with uniform strain through the thickness
Thermal cycling of the film on silica: TEC mismatch imposes in-plane compression on heating and tension on cooling
On heating, strain heterogeneity in the grain grows mainly along x and falls back quasi-reversibly on cooling; it stays uniform along z
Among g1's neighbours, g3 and g6 are strongly misoriented in-plane from g1, while g2, g4 and g5 are nearly aligned with it
Single-grain out-of-plane strain vs temperature departs from the thermoelastic slope with hysteresis, and after the first heating it follows the film average

requires_unseen: Lab cycle = film average over many (111) grains (caption)

nodes.label: Dislocations cannot cross the boundaries to the misoriented neighbours along x, so they pile up and raise x-heterogeneity; their reversible motion gives quasi-reversibility
In-situ CXD tracks the 3-D strain field of one sub-micron grain through a full thermal cycle
Temperature-dependent 3-D CXD shows that single-grain strain heterogeneity evolves anisotropically and reversibly and is set by the in-plane misorientation of neighbours
Boundaries between g1 and g3 and between g1 and g6 are strongly grooved

requires_unseen: #g1 is the unlabeled central grain in F7a (caption/F7b)

nodes.label: Differences in out-of-plane orientation give different biaxial moduli, so stress accommodation at boundaries generates the strain gradients
In this reflection geometry only the u_z displacement (one strain component) is measured; other strain tensor components are not available
Au elastic anisotropy factor is about 2.9
Thermal mismatch strain in a film on a substrate scales with the TEC difference times the temperature excursion
Scherrer size broadening: delta q_size = 2 pi / L sets the width expected from grain shape alone
Oversampled coherent diffraction allows phase retrieval, and the inverse Fourier transform gives the displacement field
Cross-section SEM: grain boundaries run from the film top to the substrate
